He played college basketball for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]]. ==Early life and education== Salmons was born on December 12, 1979, in [[Philadelphia]]. ===High school career=== In 1997, Salmons was a member of a Pennsylvania high school state championship team while playing for [[Plymouth-Whitemarsh High School]] in [[Plymouth Meeting, Pennsylvania]]. As a high school basketball player for Plymouth-Whitemarsh, he reached the 1,000 point club.{{citation needed|date=July 2019}} ===College career=== He went on to play [[college basketball]] at the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|University of Miami]], where he was a four-year starter for the Hurricanes. He started 107 consecutive games for Miami, the second longest streak in school history. He was also the first player in school history to surpass 1000 career points (1287), 600 rebounds (687), 400 assists (433), and 150 steals (192).{{cite web | url = http://www.hurricanesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28700&ATCLID=205555767 | title = Player Bio: John Salmons | website = University of Miami Athletics | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160309040733/http://www.hurricanesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28700&ATCLID=205555767 | archive-date = March 9, 2016 | url-status = dead}} ==NBA career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2002–2006)=== Salmons was drafted out of the University of Miami by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] with the 26th overall selection in the [[2002 NBA draft]]. He was then immediately traded with [[Mark Bryant (basketball)|Mark Bryant]] and the rights to [[Randy Holcomb]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for [[Speedy Claxton]]. Salmons played for the 76ers through the [[2005–06 NBA season|2006 season]], averaging 4.1 points per game. ===Sacramento Kings (2006–2009)=== Salmons was set to be acquired by the [[Toronto Raptors]] on July 13, 2006, in a sign-and-trade deal with Philadelphia. On July 21, 2006, however, there were reports that Salmons was having second thoughts about going to Toronto, and the sign and trade to Toronto was canceled.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2526850 Salmons nixes sign-and-trade deal with Raptors], Associated Press, July 22, 2006 On July 24, 2006, Salmons signed a multi-year contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].[https://www.tsn.ca/nba/news_story/?ID=172240&hubname=nba John Salmons signs with Kings], Canadian Press, July 24, 2006 On December 22, 2006, he recorded his first [[triple-double]] of his NBA career against the [[Denver Nuggets]] with 21 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists.[https://web.archive.org/web/20210417085533/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261222007 Iverson doesn't start, but Nuggets rally around the Answer] ===Chicago Bulls (2009–2010)=== Salmons and [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]] were traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] on February 18, 2009, in exchange for [[Cedric Simmons]], [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]], [[Andrés Nocioni]], and [[Michael Ruffin]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/trade_090218.html |title=Bulls acquire Miller and Salmons |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2009-02-18 |access-date=2009-02-19}} In 2009, Salmons proved to be a key contributor, helping lead the Bulls to the [[2009 NBA Playoffs]]. In Chicago, he continued to average over 18 points per game for the season. Salmons also logged a whopping 44.7 minutes per game in the playoffs, in part because there were a combined seven overtime periods in the Bulls' first round series against the [[Boston Celtics]]. The Bulls were eventually eliminated in game seven of that series. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2010–2011)=== [[File:Joe Johnson over John Salmons.jpg|thumb|Salmons with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], guarding [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]] of the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in February 2010]] On February 18, 2010, Salmons was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for [[Hakim Warrick]], [[Joe Alexander (basketball)|Joe Alexander]], and the Bulls' second-round picks in 2011 and 2012, with the Bucks given the option to swap first-round picks, provided it is not a top 10 pick, in the [[2010 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/salmons_trade_100218.html |title=Bucks Acquire John Salmons from Bulls |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-02-18 |access-date=2010-02-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100410042305/http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/salmons_trade_100218.html |archive-date=2010-04-10 |url-status=dead }} In Milwaukee, Salmons averaged nearly 20 points per game for the Bucks after his acquisition. He opted out of his final year of his contract but then signed a five-year deal to stay with the Bucks. ===Return to Sacramento (2011–2013)=== [[File:John Salmons Klay Thompson.jpg|thumb|Salmons with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in March 2013]] On June 23, 2011, he was traded back to the [[Sacramento Kings]] as part of a three-way deal including the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. The Kings received [[Jimmer Fredette]] in the transaction.[http://www.nba.com/2011/news/06/23/draft-trades/index.html 2011 Draft Day Trade Tracker] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110627231015/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/06/23/draft-trades/index.html |date=2011-06-27 }} ===Toronto Raptors (2013–2014)=== On December 9, 2013, the Kings traded Salmons, [[Greivis Vásquez]], [[Patrick Patterson (basketball)|Patrick Patterson]], and [[Chuck Hayes]] to the [[Toronto Raptors]] for [[Rudy Gay]], [[Quincy Acy]], and [[Aaron Gray]].{{cite news|url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-kings-120913/|title=Raptors Acquire Vasquez, Salmons, Hayes & Patterson From Kings|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2013|access-date=December 9, 2013|archive-date=December 12, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212075336/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-kings-120913/|url-status=dead}} On June 30, 2014, Salmons was traded, along with a 2015 second-round pick, to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Lou Williams|Louis Williams]] and the draft rights to [[Lucas Nogueira]].[http://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-second-round-pick-and-salmons-toronto Hawks Acquire 2015 Second Round Pick and Salmons from Toronto] On July 10, 2014, he was waived by the Hawks.[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-john-salmons Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on John Salmons] ===New Orleans Pelicans (2014–2015)=== On August 26, 2014, Salmons signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-john-salmons Pelicans Sign John Salmons] In Salmons' final NBA game on February 2, 2015, a 115–100 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]], he played for only {{frac|7|1|2}} minutes and recorded no points and only one assist. On February 19, 2015, Salmons was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] as a part of a three-team deal with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-stockpile-draft-picks-trade-heat|title=Suns Stockpile Draft Picks in Trade with Heat|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}} Later that month, Salmons and [[Kendall Marshall]] were both waived.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-barron-10-day-contract|title=Suns Sign Barron to 10-Day
